label: Sequence starts with b: original-phase steps t>=3 and the <DEL> step
explanation: Fires when the first original token is b (97% of activation mass falls in such sequences). It turns on from step 3 onward, stays on through the rest of the original phase, and also fires on the <DEL> step, which is where b gets output. It is essentially silent in the copy phase (0.1% of mass) and at steps 0-2. Which token is the current input barely matters. Activation is highest in the middle of the original phase (t=4-6) and drops off toward the end of long sequences. The strongest examples begin with b b, but those sequences are too rare to account for much mass. The missed activations are weak, scattered firings in sequences that do not start with b, often ones with b in position 1. A few false positives are steps right after another b input or late steps (t=8-9) in long sequences.

issues: Minor: the misses are not purely scattered. About 13% of active steps (count recall 0.134) come from sequences with orig(1)==b and first_tok!=b at t>=3. The firings there are weak (0.028 of mass) and imprecise (precision 0.17). The explanation already says this ('often ones with b in position 1'). Adding it to the predicate drops test F1 to 0.72 (precision 0.59), so it does not belong in the main predicate.
Count recall is 0.81, but the lowest activation quartile has only 0.28 coverage. The predicate covers the top three quartiles at 0.97 to 1.0, so the gap sits entirely in weak activations.
False-positive classes are small and match the explanation. When orig(2)==b, precision is 0.77 (2358 predicted steps). Late steps t>=8 still have precision 0.93.

The factual claims hold on the dev profile. Steps 0-2 have 0 activations. The copy phase holds 0.001 of mass and the delimiter 0.159. Mass peaks at t=4 (0.278) and t=5 (0.239), then falls to 0.010 at t=9. Lift by input token is about 1.0x across all letters and digits. On the test split, first_tok==b in the copy phase has precision 0.0009.
